s: PostgreSQL extended into a time-series powerhouse: hypertables auto-partition time and compress history.
w: Tables become hypertables chunked by time (and optionally space). Recent chunks stay hot on disk/RAM; older ones compress 10-20x and can tier to cheap storage. Continuous aggregates maintain rollups incrementally (1-min/1-hour averages) instead of recomputing dashboards. Full Postgres SQL + joins still available.
use: Infrastructure/app metrics with retention policies (raw 7d, rollups 1y)
IoT sensor ingestion at steady high insert rates
Event telemetry where SQL analytics matter later
Fleet tracking (GPS breadcrumbs) with windowed queries
avoid: Tag cardinality in the millions (influx-style TSDBs handle differently; watch index bloat)
General OLTP mixing (keep separate from transactional DB)

pat.d: Raw events -> continuous aggregates -> dashboard reads.

pits: High-cardinality tags explode indexes - bucket IDs, normalize dimensions
Compression jobs lag ingest - size background workers
tips: Sell 'just Postgres': existing skills/backups apply; compare with influx (simpler but less SQL) and clickhouse (faster scans, heavier ops)
